learning_outcomes.text: Recognition of Career Centers and Activities: Ensuring that the student is aware of the services offered by the Career Center and establishing a link between the Career Center and the student.
Increasing Self-Awareness: The student; learning concepts such as intelligence, personality, knowledge, skill, talent and competence and establishing the connection of these concepts with career.

Exploring Career Options: Students get to know sectors such as the public sector, private sector, academia, non-governmental organizations, understand the differences between sectors and see the working life in these sectors.
Developing Fine Skills: Increasing awareness about the importance of developing fine skills in the career process.
Exploring Activities to Contribute to Career Planning: Informing students about activities that can contribute to their careers outside of their courses throughout their university life.

Recognition of International Exchange Programs: Students' awareness of the contributions of international exchange programs to personal development and academic life and their positive reflections on their career plans.

Recognition of Talent Gate: The student learns that through Talent Gate, counseling can be obtained from Career Centers, applications can be made to activities such as fairs, seminars, workshops, and internship announcements.

syllabus_topics: YOUR CAREER JOURNEY STARTS FIRST STOP: CAREER CENTER What is a career planning course? What is a career center? What are the issues that the career center will benefit from? How to benefit from Career Centers?
INTELLIGENCE AND PERSONALITY; What is intelligence and personality? How do intelligence and personality relate to career?
PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS; What are the concepts of knowledge, skill, talent, competence? What is the connection between these concepts and career?
THE KEY TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE ON YOUR CAREER PATH: SKILLS What are fine skills and technical skills? Why do students need these skills?
WHAT IS CAREER? Explanation of career and career-related concepts. What do you think career is? So what is it actually?
HOW DO I PREPARE FOR MY CAREER? Explaining the activities that students can do to contribute to their careers throughout their university life. (Academic, social, artistic and sports activities)
INDUSTRY DAYS - NGO'S NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS National non-governmental organizations activities and volunteer work opportunities. Advice from NGO staff to students on how to spend their college life.

INDUSTRY DAYS - NGO'S NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS National non-governmental organizations activities and volunteer work opportunities. Advice from NGO staff to students on how to spend their college life. Doctors of the Earth (interview and institution activities) United Nations (interview and institution activities) The student's research and writing about which NGO they want to work in.

SECTOR DAYS PUBLIC SECTOR Engagement from public sector workers about career stories and advice to students on how to spend their college life Career stories from interns and employees in the public sector

SECTOR DAYS- PRIVATE SECTOR Information from private sector employees about their career stories and advice to students on how they should spend their university life Career stories from interns and employees at different levels in the private sector

INDUSTRY DAYS ACADEMY Informing students about the career stories of academicians and Advice on how they should spend their university life at different levels in academia career stories from employees

SECTOR DAYS ENTREPRENEURSHIP Information about the career stories of entrepreneurs and advice to students on how to spend their university life Entrepreneurship stories "Do you dream of an entrepreneurship story?" Preparing an article by researching the question.
TALENT GATE I WRITE MY FIRST BIOGRAPHY What is the Talent Gate? What is the benefit for students? How is the skill gate used? How should the resume be?
COURSE ASSESSMENT In this course, students will evaluate the course with the appraisal form prepared by the Presidential Human Resources Office.
